rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Biodiversity loss — causes and consequences ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Biodiversity loss — causes and consequences** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Biodiversity and Conservation fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Species are disappearing at 100–1000× the natural background rate. The driving causes are summarised as the **four major causes**: habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, and co-extinctions. The consequences are not just sad stories — losing species erodes ecosystem services, narrows the genetic bank for food and medicine, and destabilises the systems that produce our food and…

rows.text: Trick 1: The 'evil quartet': habitat loss/fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasion, co-extinctions — four causes, four marks.  ·  Trick 2: Alien species examples: Lantana, water hyacinth (Eichhornia), Parthenium, Nile perch in Lake Victoria — quote two.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) List the four major causes of biodiversity loss with one example each. (2) Why is habitat fragmentation worse than simple area loss? (3) Define co-extinction with an example. (4) Give three consequences of biodiversity loss for humans. (5) Which cause dominates globally?  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Biodiversity is being lost to four human-driven causes — habitat loss, over-exploitation, invasions, co-extinctions — and the bill arrives as lost services, lost options and lost stability. **Self-check:** can you match water hyacinth, rhino poaching and fig wasps to their correct causes?
